---
title: "Direct sampling & plots"
sidebar: start
---












Every distribution in `m.dist` can be sampled **directly**, outside of a model, by passing
`sample=True`. This is useful for prior predictive checks, simulating data, or quickly inspecting a
distribution's shape.

```python
from BayesForge import bf
m = bf()
# Draw 1000 samples from a standard normal
x = m.dist.normal(0, 1, shape=(1000,), sample=True)
```

## What `sample=True` returns

By default (`to_jax=False`) a direct sample is returned as a **`SampledData`** object — a thin wrapper
around a JAX array. It behaves like a JAX array everywhere (arithmetic, indexing, `jnp.*` functions,
`jit`/`vmap`/`grad`, use as a distribution parameter), and its `repr` reports the dtype so you can see
the kind and precision at a glance:

```python
from BayesForge import bf
m = bf()
x = m.dist.normal(0, 1, shape=(3,), sample=True)
x        # SampledData([ 0.63, 0.29, -0.40], dtype=float64)
```

The extra thing a `SampledData` gives you over a raw array is a set of **built-in plotting methods**.

If you only want the raw JAX array (no wrapper, no plotting helpers), pass `to_jax=True`:

```python
x = m.dist.normal(0, 1, shape=(1000,), sample=True, to_jax=True)   # plain jax array
```

## Plotting a sampled array

Each plotting method is called directly on the sampled object. Most accept `interactive=True`
(the default, **Plotly**) or `interactive=False` (**matplotlib / seaborn**):

```python
s = m.dist.normal(0, 1, shape=(1000, 4), sample=True)   # 2D: [n_samples, n_variables]

s.hist()                        # interactive Plotly histogram
s.violinplot(interactive=False) # static matplotlib
s.corr_heatmap()
```

The available methods depend on the **shape** of the sampled array.

## 2D — `(n_samples, n_variables)`

The most common case: several variables sampled together.

```python
s = m.dist.normal(0, 1, shape=(1000, 4), sample=True)

s.hist()          # one histogram trace per column
s.density()       # KDE per column (Plotly only)
s.boxplot()       # one box per column
s.violinplot()    # violin + box + mean line per column
s.pairplot()      # pairwise scatter (max_vars=5)
s.corr_heatmap()  # annotated correlation matrix (digits=5)
s.traceplot()     # MCMC-style line per column
s.autocorr()      # autocorrelation per column
s.ridgeline()     # stacked densities (category_labels=, offset=2)
s.surface_3d()    # surface plot (Plotly only)
```

## Time series — `(n_samples, n_time)`

Treat the second axis as time and summarise across draws.

```python
s = m.dist.gaussian_random_walk(scale=0.5, num_steps=50, shape=(500,), sample=True)

s.timeseries(credible_interval=0.9)   # posterior mean + credible band
```

## 3D — `(n_samples, n_groups, n_times)`

```python
s.hist()          # 3D ridged histograms across groups / times
s.ridgeline()     # also accepts 3D input
```

## Posterior predictive

Compare draws against observed data.

```python
# s has shape [n_draws, n_observations]
s.ppc_plot(observed_data, n_samples_to_plot=50)   # Plotly only
```

## 3D scatter — `(n_samples, >=3)`

```python
s.scatter3d()     # 3D point cloud of the first three columns
```

:::

## A non-plot helper

Alongside the plots, `SampledData` exposes the highest-density interval:

```python
low, high = s.hdi(cred_mass=0.95)
```

## Notes & gotchas

::: callout-note
- `density`, `surface_3d`, and `ppc_plot` are **Plotly-only** — passing `interactive=False` has no
  effect on them.
- The dimensional requirement is **enforced**: e.g. `corr_heatmap`, `boxplot`, `violinplot`,
  `pairplot`, `traceplot`, `scatter3d`, and `timeseries` raise a `ValueError` if the array is not the
  expected shape.
- Plotting methods live on the `SampledData` wrapper only. If you sampled with `to_jax=True` (or later
  called `.to_jax()`), convert back with `SampledData(arr)` to plot, or re-sample without `to_jax`.
:::
